final_message:
I wrote the answer to `answer.json` in the repo root. I didn't modify any other files or run the test suite.

1. **Timestamp unit: milliseconds.** `report_usage` takes an `EpochMillis` timestamp (`billing/usage.py`). When none is given, it uses `to_millis(ctx.clock.now())`. Billing periods are stored in seconds, and `records_in_period` converts them with `to_millis` before comparing.

2. **Boundaries: start inclusive, end exclusive.** `records_in_period` keeps a record when `start <= record["timestamp"] < end`. A record exactly at the period start counts in that period. A record exactly at the period end falls into the next period.

3. **Billing timing: in arrears.** `invoices.py` documents "Licensed items are billed in advance, metered items in arrears." Metered lines are skipped when there is no usage period. On renewal, `engine._renew` passes the just-ended period as the usage period, so the usage line appears on the invoice that follows the period.

steps.command: git ls-files | head -200 && grep -rniE "timestamp|period|invoice|arrear|advance" --include=*.py . | grep -v .venv | head -150

cat billing/usage.py && grep -niE "arrear|advance|period|invoice" billing/engine.py billing/subscriptions.py billing/invoices.py billing/models.py billing/clock.py billing/money.py README.md | head -120
cat billing/clock.py && grep -n "EpochMillis\|EpochSeconds" billing/models.py | head -3 && sed -n 98,140p billing/invoices.py && sed -n 68,88p billing/engine.py
